newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end down on new issue quota.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end down on new issue quota.

text.p: Shanghai's A and B shares ended down sharply on Friday after Beijing announced a huge new quota for stock issues in 1997 and suspended two companies for investigation into price fluctuations, brokers said.
The B share index fell 4.332 points or 4.88 percent to 84.438 points on volume of 25.23 million shares worth $18.076 million.
The A share index plunged 107.333 points or 7.24 percent to 1,375.91 on volume of 886.374 million shares worth 12.188 billion yuan.
The official media reported that the issue quota for 1997 has been set at 30 billion shares.
During the afternoon session, the Shanghai Stock Exchange announced the suspension of trading of two A share companies because of abnormal fluctuations in their share prices.
"The two measures showed the government's strong determination to curb the stock markets, which resulted in panic selling," said one broker.
"Controls are necessary given the recent feverish market sentiment," another broker said. "Further steps to rein in the market are expected."
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded, with 37 down, three flat and one up.
Tientsin Marine Shipping was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling, plunging $0.064 or 9.93 percent to $0.580 on volume of 1.1 million shares.

The market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development was the most actively traded on heavy selling despite institutional support, falling $0.054 or 3.72 percent to $1.396 on volume of 3.9 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index plunged on the same negative factors, and market sentiment was hurt greatly, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index slumped 290.891 points or 7.13 percent to 3,786.586 points.
Qinhuangdao Yaohua Glass was the biggest loser on institutional unwinding selling, diving 0.94 yuan or 10.04 percent to 8.42 yuan on volume of 4.2 million shares.
